As for the definition of "zero-shot generalization" in the context of text-to-image AIs, it seems sensible. The concept of zero-shot generalization refers to the ability of a model to apply its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts without requiring additional training data. In the context of text-to-image AIs, this means that the model can generate images based on text prompts without needing to see examples of the specific image class or concept before.

The 2013 paper cited in the response likely discussed the theoretical foundations of zero-shot generalization in AI, and its application to text-to-image AIs is a natural extension of this concept. By enabling text-to-image AIs to generalize to new, unseen concepts, zero-shot generalization has the potential to significantly improve the performance and versatility of these models.

It's worth noting that zero-shot generalization is a challenging problem in AI, and achieving it requires the development of sophisticated models that can effectively learn and apply abstract knowledge.
